reason: Decides whether `update` rejects `--bootstrap` as an unknown argument instead of parsing it.
Caller receives Err naming the rejected argument rather than a parsed UpdateArgs.
Decides whether the run may proceed or is refused with EXIT_NEEDS_TERMINAL.
Without a terminal the caller observes EXIT_NEEDS_TERMINAL instead of None.
A no-terminal run returns the refusal code immediately before any lookup or change.
A missing release dir makes run() return that code before touching the flow.
When deps cannot be built the run aborts with exit 1 instead of continuing.
The process-deps failure is signaled to the caller as exit code 1.
The restart logic later reads this command to decide how the new program is started.
The resumed-run check is acted on before the not-set-up check that directly follows it, so a resumed run never reports NOT_SET_UP.
A restarted run goes straight to finish() instead of the normal update questions.
Without an install record the session says NOT_SET_UP and exits instead of checking for updates.
Caller observes EXIT_NOT_SET_UP when there is no install record.
The stored newest release drives the Unknown and newer-release checks that follow.
The Unknown check runs before the newer-release check, so an unknown newest exits 1 rather than being reported as up to date.
Unknown newest release means nothing is changed and the exit code is 1.
The unknown-newest path is signaled to the caller as exit code 1.
When no newer release exists the session prints up-to-date and exits 0 instead of asking.
Answering no (or end of input) changes nothing and exits with EXIT_CANCELLED.
Declining the update prompt is signaled as EXIT_CANCELLED.
A refusal (e.g. no trusted key) prints the note and exits 1 instead of downloading.
The update refusal is signaled to the caller as exit code 1.
Decides whether the underlying failure reason is printed before the generic failure note.
When there is no bootstrap offer the function returns None so the normal menu opens instead.
Declining the bootstrap offer keeps everything and returns EXIT_CANCELLED.
The declined bootstrap offer is signaled as Some(EXIT_CANCELLED).
Planning the recorded choices changes what finish() later applies and reports.
With nothing to change besides the program, only the check results are printed; otherwise the changes are listed and confirmed.
Decides whether the updated() line is printed before the changes-needed listing.
Declining the apply prompt keeps the files and exits with EXIT_CANCELLED.
Declining the changes is signaled to the caller as EXIT_CANCELLED.
Applies the planned update, whose results the following lines and exit code report.
Decides whether the DONE line is appended to the result output.
Pure function of self; dropping or altering a field changes what run() passes on.
Effect-only wrapper; every user-visible line goes through it.
Effect-only prompt writer; without the flush the question would not appear before the blocking read.
Only prints the review view; it changes no state, so its output is all a caller sees.
Pure computation from the flow; the lines it returns are exactly what the user is shown after applying.
